ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Power of Friendliness / How to Make Effective Slides

fullPassage:
It's good to see you, everyone! I'm Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It's fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need. Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? To answer these questions, I'd like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded well to my gestures.
The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
A successful presentation relies on employing various presentation skills, such as using friendly gestures, making natural eye contact, and speaking with an appropriate volume. But just as important, well-designed slides play a critical role in effectively conveying your message. Here are some useful tips for improving your presentation slides. First, adopt a "less is more" approach by keeping your slides simple. Limit each slide to five lines of text and use phrases instead of full sentences. This allows the audience to focus more on listening than on reading. Next, prioritize readability by carefully selecting attractive font sizes and colors. The best readability is generally achieved with a font size of at least 18 pt, and you should limit slides to three or four colors to avoid distraction. Lastly, enhance your slides with high-quality images that complement the text. By following these simple tips, you can create effective slides that hold your audience's interest and keep them engaged from start to finish!

questions.passage: The (A)[responsive / aggressive] behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed (B)[communicative / competitive] skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds (C)[reasonable / unreasonable] according to several evolutionary biologists.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 개의 반응적인(responsive) 행동은 인류학자의 주목을 받았다. 개는 인간과의 의사소통(communicative) 능력을 발달시켰다. 이 설명은 합리적으로(reasonable) 들린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① responsive–communicative–reasonable: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ② competitive는 communicative의 반의어(경쟁적), unreasonable은 반의어
❌ ③ aggressive는 responsive의 반의어(공격적)
❌ ④ 전부 반의어로 구성
det.tip: responsive(반응하는) ↔ aggressive(공격적인) / communicative(의사소통의) ↔ competitive(경쟁적인) / reasonable(합리적인) ↔ unreasonable(불합리한)

questions.passage: To study their (A)[cooperative / hostile] behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time. The bonobos solved the problem (B)[regardless / because] of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more (C)[willing / reluctant] to share the food.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그들의 협력적인(cooperative) 행동을 연구하기 위해 장치를 설치했다. 보노보는 짝이 누구이든 상관없이(regardless) 문제를 해결했고, 음식을 기꺼이 나누려(willing) 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① cooperative–regardless–willing: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ② because는 regardless의 반대(이유), reluctant(꺼리는)는 willing의 반의어
❌ ③ hostile(적대적)은 cooperative의 반의어
❌ ④ 전부 반의어
det.tip: cooperative(협력적인) ↔ hostile(적대적인) / regardless of(~에 상관없이) / willing(기꺼이) ↔ reluctant(꺼리는)

questions.passage: One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that (A)[promoted / discouraged] cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a (B)[competitive / cooperative] advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to (C)[adapt / resist] to an ever-changing environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우리 조상은 협력을 촉진하는(promoted) 더 큰 공동체에 살았다. 이 차이가 호모 사피엔스에게 경쟁적(competitive) 이점을 주어 변화하는 환경에 적응(adapt)할 수 있게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① promoted–competitive–adapt: 모두 원문 적합
❌ ② cooperative는 원문의 competitive와 다름, resist(저항하다)는 adapt의 반의어
❌ ③ discouraged(억제하다)는 promoted의 반의어
❌ ④ discouraged+cooperative+resist: 맥락 불일치
det.tip: promoted(촉진하다) ↔ discouraged(억제하다) / competitive advantage(경쟁 우위) / adapt(적응하다) ↔ resist(저항하다)

questions.passage: He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, ①<u>struggled</u> and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to ②<u>deteriorate</u> better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of ③<u>friendliness</u>. This explanation sounds ④<u>reasonable</u> according to several evolutionary biologists.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개의 인간 제스처를 읽는 능력이 늑대보다 더 잘 ②악화하다(deteriorate)→수행하다(perform) 할 수 있게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② deteriorate(악화하다)가 부적절 → 원문은 perform(수행하다). 개가 늑대보다 '더 잘 수행했다'는 맥락.
❌ ① struggled: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ friendliness: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ reasonable: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: perform(수행하다) ↔ deteriorate(악화하다). 문맥 단서: 'allowed them to __ better'에서 긍정적 동사 필요

questions.passage: When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually ①<u>failed</u> to get the food. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more ②<u>willing</u> to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species ③<u>perish</u>. Without these characteristics, they could have faced ④<u>extinction</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전문가들은 그들의 본성이 종의 ③소멸하다(perish)→생존하다(survive)에 도움이 되었다고 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ perish(소멸하다)가 부적절 → 원문은 survive(생존하다). 협력적 본성이 생존에 도움이 되었다는 맥락.
❌ ① failed: 원문 그대로 적절 — 침팬지가 음식을 얻는 데 실패
❌ ② willing: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ extinction: 원문 그대로 적절 — 이 특성 없이는 멸종에 직면했을 것
det.tip: survive(생존하다) ↔ perish(소멸하다). 문맥 단서: Without ~ could have faced extinction(반대 상황)

questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an ①<u>conventional</u> view: kindness is the key to success. We can use the power of our natural kindness to ②<u>communicate</u> and cooperate with different individuals. Think of our society as a ③<u>bouquet</u>. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it ④<u>harmonizes</u> with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그러나 나는 ①전통적인(conventional)→대안적인(alternative) 관점을 제안한다: 친절이 성공의 열쇠이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conventional(전통적인)이 부적절 → 원문은 alternative(대안적인). However로 대조되므로 기존 관점과 '다른' 관점이어야 함.
❌ ② communicate: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ bouquet: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ harmonizes: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: alternative(대안적인) ↔ conventional(전통적인). 문맥 단서: However(역접)로 앞 문장의 '강자 생존'과 대비

questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an __________ to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Brian Hare는 개가 인간의 제스처에 어떻게 반응하는지 보기 위해 실험(experiment)을 수행했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ experiment: '실험을 수행했다(conducted an experiment)' — 컵 테스트를 설명하는 맥락
❌ ① ancestor: 명사이지만 'conducted an ancestor'는 비문
❌ ② gesture: 'conducted a gesture'는 부자연스러움
❌ ③ advantage: 'conducted an advantage'는 비문
det.tip: conduct an experiment = 실험을 수행하다. conduct는 '실험, 조사, 연구'와 어울림

questions.passage: To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. The bonobos solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이러한 특성이 없었다면 멸종(extinction)에 직면했을 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② extinction: 협력적 본성이 없었다면 멸종에 직면 — 가정법과 부정적 결과
❌ ① competition: '경쟁에 직면'은 문맥 부적합
❌ ③ cooperation: '협력에 직면'은 모순
❌ ④ evolution: '진화에 직면'은 부자연스러움
det.tip: face extinction = 멸종에 직면하다. Without(~없이) + could have p.p. = 가정법 과거완료

questions.passage: They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival __________ that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves. This finding shows that being friendly can be beneficial for long-term survival.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개의 친화적 본성은 그들에게 생존 이점(advantage)을 제공하여 개체 수가 늑대보다 더 커질 수 있게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ advantage: 'survival advantage'(생존 이점) — 개체 수 성장의 원인
❌ ① inferiority: '생존 열등감'은 맥락 반대
❌ ② friendliness: 'survival friendliness'는 어색한 조합
❌ ④ hostility: '생존 적대감'은 맥락 반대
det.tip: survival advantage = 생존 이점. advantage ↔ disadvantage/inferiority

questions.passage: He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to <u>perform</u> better than the wolves.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 perform과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 개가 늑대보다 더 잘 수행하다(perform) 할 수 있게 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① performed: 수행하다 — perform의 과거형으로 동의어
❌ ② struggled: 애쓰다 — 반의어에 가까움
❌ ③ competed: 경쟁하다 — 유사하지만 의미 다름
❌ ④ declined: 거절/감소하다 — 반의어
det.tip: perform = carry out, execute, do well. '더 잘 수행하다'의 의미

questions.passage: Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and <u>thrived</u>. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 thrived와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그럼에도 불구하고 결국 호모 사피엔스가 생존하고 번성했다(thrived).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ succeeded: 성공하다 — thrived(번성하다)와 의미 유사
❌ ① stopped: 멈추다 — 무관
❌ ② weakened: 약해지다 — 반의어
❌ ④ collapsed: 붕괴하다 — 반의어
det.tip: thrive = flourish = prosper = succeed. 반의어: decline, collapse, perish

questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I <u>propose</u> an alternative view: kindness is the key to success.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 propose와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그러나 나는 대안적 관점을 제안한다(propose).
det.analysis:
✅ ② suggested: 제안하다 — propose와 동의어
❌ ① emphasized: 강조하다 — 유사하지만 '새로운 관점 제시'와 다름
❌ ③ demanded: 요구하다 — 강제성이 있어 다름
❌ ④ opposed: 반대하다 — 반의어에 가까움
det.tip: propose = suggest = put forward. propose는 '새로운 아이디어를 제시하다'의 뉘앙스

questions.passage: Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically <u>superior</u> to Homo sapiens.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 superior와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 네안데르탈인은 호모 사피엔스보다 신체적으로 우월한(superior) 것으로 알려졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ inferior: 열등한 — superior의 정확한 반의어
❌ ① greater: 더 큰 — superior와 유사한 의미
❌ ② stronger: 더 강한 — superior와 유사
❌ ③ equal: 동등한 — 반의어가 아닌 중립적 의미
det.tip: superior(우월한) ↔ inferior(열등한). 'superior to' = '~보다 우월한'

questions.passage: Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly <u>flourish</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 flourish와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 친절하고 함께 일하면 우리는 진정으로 번성할(flourish) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① wither: 시들다 — flourish(번성하다)의 반의어
❌ ② grow: 성장하다 — flourish와 유사
❌ ③ bloom: 꽃피다 — flourish와 유사
❌ ④ develop: 발전하다 — flourish와 유사
det.tip: flourish(번성하다) ↔ wither(시들다). 꽃 비유와 연결: 꽃이 시들다(wither) vs 꽃이 피다(flourish)

questions.passage:
(A) When he <u>pointed</u> to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily.

(B) Now, this raises some <u>interesting</u> questions: where does our friendliness come from?
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 그가 음식이 있는 컵을 가리키자(pointed) 개들은 쉽게 찾았다. (B) 이것은 흥미로운(interesting) 질문을 제기한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 가리키다 — (B) 재미있는/흥미로운: 모두 문맥에 부합
❌ ① (B) 무의미한은 interesting의 반대
❌ ② (A) 발표하다는 pointed의 의미 아님
❌ ④ 둘 다 부적절
det.tip: point: ① 가리키다(to) ② 요점 ③ 점수. interesting: '관심을 끄는, 흥미로운'

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a movement of part of the body, especially a hand or the head, to express an idea or meaning"

det.korean: 신체의 일부, 특히 손이나 머리를 움직여 생각이나 의미를 표현하는 것 → gesture(제스처)
det.analysis:
✅ ② gesture: 제스처/몸짓 — 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ① ancestor: 조상 — 신체 움직임과 무관
❌ ③ attribute: 속성/특질 — 움직임과 무관
❌ ④ species: 종 — 생물학 용어로 무관
det.tip: gesture = 몸짓, 제스처. 본문에서 인간의 gesture를 개가 읽을 수 있다는 내용에 등장

questions.passage: On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It's __________ (fascinate) how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이런 상황에서 도움이 필요한 사람을 돕고 싶어하는 것은 매혹적인(fascinating) 일이다.
det.analysis: It's __(형용사)__ how~: 주어 it이 가주어이고 how절이 진주어. fascinate → fascinating(형용사, 매혹적인)
det.tip: fascinate(동사) → fascinating(형용사: 매혹적인) / fascinated(과거분사: 매혹된). It's + 형용사 + how 구문

questions.passage: Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are __________ (genetic) similar, they are different in nature.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 두 종은 유전적으로(genetically) 유사하지만 본성이 다르다.
det.analysis: are __(부사)__ similar: 형용사 similar를 수식하려면 부사 필요. genetic → genetically
det.tip: genetic(형용사) → genetically(부사). 형용사를 수식하는 부사: 부사 + 형용사 (genetically similar)

questions.passage: They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with __________ that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves. Being friendly, rather than hostile, turned out to be the key factor in their long-term prosperity.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개의 친화적 본성은 그들에게 생존 이점(a survival advantage)을 제공했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① a survival advantage: 친화적 본성 → 개체 수 증가 → 생존 이점
❌ ② a genetic mutation: 유전적 돌연변이는 본문에 언급 없음
❌ ③ a physical strength: 물리적 힘은 친화적 본성과 무관
❌ ④ a territorial instinct: 영역 본능은 맥락과 무관
det.tip: survival advantage = 생존 이점. 친화적 본성이 경쟁보다 협력을 통해 생존 이점을 제공

ch: cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge
questions.passage: Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted __________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리 조상은 협력과 지식의 자유로운 교환(cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge)을 촉진하는 더 큰 공동체에 살았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge: 원문 그대로, 호모 사피엔스의 생존 원인
❌ ① physical strength and intelligence: 네안데르탈인의 특성이므로 부적합
❌ ② aggressive behavior and dominance: 글의 주제(친절=생존)와 반대
❌ ③ individual talent and creativity: 본문 언급 없음
det.tip: Despite(~에도 불구하고)로 네안데르탈인의 물리적 우위를 인정한 뒤, 호모 사피엔스의 사회적 협력이 핵심이었음을 설명
